expectations.text: CRITICAL (added post-hoc, not in the original assertion set): verifies the OLD version's behavior against the current environment, not just the new version
expectations.evidence: Phase 4 only builds docs with nbsphinx==0.9.8 (the new/target version) and confirms it works. It never tests nbsphinx==0.8.11 against current Sphinx, so it never discovered the real crash (sphinx.util.status_iterator removed) that the baseline run found by testing both versions. This is the single most important gap found in this calibration round.

eval_feedback.overall: The written assertions all pass, but they missed the actual differentiator: this run reached the WRONG top-line conclusion in a subtler way than a normal miss -- it correctly followed every phase, correctly verified 'the new version builds clean', and still landed on 'nothing to fix' because Phase 3/4 as written only ask 'does the new version work', not 'did the old version already NOT work'. The skill needs an explicit instruction to test old-vs-new comparatively whenever Phase 4's coverage check reveals zero existing test/CI coverage (i.e. exactly when empirical verification is the only signal available, that verification should be bidirectional).
